problems.title: Greatest three-digit multiple of seven
problems.question: Find the greatest three-digit number divisible by 7.
problems.idea: Start below 1000 and find the last multiple of seven.
formulas: A multiple of 7 has form 7k for integer k.
steps: The next multiple already has four digits.
Therefore 994 is the greatest allowed multiple.

problems.title: Two successive ten-percent price reductions
problems.question: Shoes cost 300 lari on August 3. On the first day of each following month their price falls by 10%. Find their price on October 7 of the same year.
problems.idea: Each reduction multiplies the current price by 0.9.
steps: The first reduction occurs on September 1, giving 300·0.9=270.
The second occurs on October 1, giving 270·0.9=243.
There is no further reduction before October 7.

problems.title: Midpoint distance across a line
problems.question: The ends of segment AB are 5 cm and 3 cm from line a, and AB crosses a. Find its midpoint’s distance from a.
problems.idea: Use signed distances because the endpoints lie on opposite sides.
formulas: Signed distance to a fixed line is a linear function of coordinates.
The midpoint’s signed distance is the average of the two endpoint signed distances.
steps: Give the two endpoint distances signs +5 and -3.
The midpoint’s signed distance is (5-3)/2=1.
Take its absolute value to obtain the ordinary distance.

problems.title: Largest perimeter of a similar triangle
problems.question: A triangle has sides 7,10,12. In a similar triangle one side exceeds another by 10 cm. Find the greatest possible perimeter.
problems.idea: A similarity multiplies side differences and perimeter by the same scale.
formulas: Scaled difference=k·original difference; scaled perimeter=k·original perimeter.
steps: The positive side differences are 10-7=3, 12-10=2, and 12-7=5.
To obtain difference 10, the possible scale factors are 10/3,5,2.
The largest is 5. The original perimeter is 29, so the greatest new perimeter is 5·29=145.

problems.title: Determine a parameter in a composition
problems.question: f(x)=2x+1, g(x)=x²-a and f(g(x))=2x²-3. Find a.
problems.idea: Substitute g into f and compare constant terms.
steps: The composition is 2(x²-a)+1=2x²-2a+1.
Its constant must equal -3, so -2a+1=-3.
Thus a=2.

problems.title: More than two roots require an identity
problems.question: For which a does (a²-6a+8)x²+(a²-4)x+10-3a-a²=0 have more than two solutions?
problems.idea: A polynomial of degree at most two can have more than two roots only if all coefficients vanish.
steps: The three coefficients share the factor a-2.
Their other factors vanish at different values, so only a=2 makes all three zero.
At a=2 the equation is 0=0 and every real x solves it.

problems.title: A common point of three function graphs
problems.question: The graphs y=f(x), y=g(x), y=f(x)+g(x) share point M. What must be true of M?
problems.idea: At the same input, their equal output must equal twice itself.
steps: Substitute the first two equalities into the third: v+v=v.
This gives v=0.
The point’s y-coordinate is zero, so it lies on the x-axis.
problems.answer: M lies on the x-axis (option ა).

problems.title: An isosceles trapezoid with two equal-length conditions
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has each leg equal to the smaller base and each diagonal equal to the larger base. Find its acute angle.
problems.idea: Use two isosceles triangles formed by a diagonal.
formulas: Triangle angles sum to 180°; base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
Angles along a trapezoid leg sum to 180°.
steps: Label the trapezoid A-B-C-D with AD the larger base. Let each acute base angle be θ.
AB=BC, so triangle ABC has vertex angle at B equal to 180°-θ and base angles at A,C equal to θ/2.
Thus ∠CAD=θ-θ/2=θ/2.
AC=AD, so triangle ACD has equal angles at C,D. The angle at D is θ, giving θ+θ+θ/2=180°.
Therefore θ=72°.

problems.title: Simplify an absolute-value quotient using signs
problems.question: x<0 and y>0. Simplify (x²-2xy+y²)/|x-y|.
problems.idea: The numerator is a square, and x-y is strictly negative.
steps: Because x<0<y, x-y<0 and is nonzero.
The quotient is |x-y|.
For a negative quantity, |x-y|=-(x-y)=y-x.

problems.title: Maximise a product over a finite set
problems.question: Each of x,y,z is chosen from {-3,1/2,2}. Find the greatest value of (x/y)z².
problems.idea: Maximise a positive quotient and the nonnegative squared factor.
formulas: All possible y values are nonzero; z²≤9.
steps: A negative quotient gives a negative expression, so it cannot beat a positive attainable value.
The greatest positive quotient is 2/(1/2)=4; the quotient from two negative entries is only 1.
The greatest z² is (-3)²=9. These choices can be made together.
The maximum is 4·9=36.

problems.title: Area change after a square’s side grows
problems.question: A square’s side is increased by 20%. By what percentage does its area grow?
problems.idea: Area scales as the square of the side factor.
formulas: If side changes by factor k, square area changes by k².
steps: The new side is 1.2 times the old one.
The area factor is 1.2²=1.44.
The increase is 0.44 of the original area, or 44%.

problems.title: Triangle area using an extended square side
problems.question: A square ABCD has side 6 cm. E is on the extension of AD, with DE=BD. Find area BDE.
problems.idea: Use DE as the triangle base; its line is AD.
steps: The perpendicular distance from B to the line AD is 6.

problems.title: Work rate of a more powerful plant
problems.question: One power station produces electricity at three times the rate of the other. How long would the first need to produce what both make in 24 days?
problems.idea: Express all production rates in units of the smaller plant’s rate.
steps: Let the second plant’s daily rate be r. The first has rate 3r, and together they have 4r.
The 24-day joint output is 96r.
The first alone needs 96r/(3r)=32 days.

problems.title: Remove absolute values by locating a radical
problems.question: Find |√8-3|+|√8-2|.
problems.idea: Use 2<√8<3 to determine both signs.
steps: √8-3 is negative, so the first term is 3-√8.
√8-2 is positive, so the second is √8-2.
Adding cancels the radicals and gives 1.

problems.title: A quadratic with exactly one solution
problems.question: For which α does αx²+2αx+3=0 have exactly one real solution?
problems.idea: Handle the zero leading coefficient before using the discriminant.
formulas: For a genuine quadratic, exactly one real root means discriminant zero.
steps: If α=0, the equation is 3=0, with no solutions.
For α≠0, the discriminant is (2α)²-4α·3=4α(α-3).
Its only allowed zero is α=3. The equation then becomes 3(x+1)²=0.

problems.title: Angle between two internal bisectors
problems.question: In triangle ABC, ∠C=50°. The A and B angle bisectors meet at O. Find ∠AOB.
problems.idea: Use the angle sum in triangle AOB.
steps: Substitute A+B=130°.
The angle is 180°-65°=115°.

problems.title: Disprove a statement with one counterexample
problems.question: Which is false? One statement claims: if -2<x<3, then 4<x²<9.
problems.idea: Squaring an interval that crosses zero does not preserve its lower endpoint.
formulas: A universal claim is false if one permitted input violates its conclusion.
steps: Choose x=0, which lies between -2 and 3.
Then x²=0, violating 4<x².
The other statements follow from subtraction order, the definition of absolute value, and squaring a number less than -3.

problems.title: Which conditions determine a quadratic’s sign?
problems.question: I: a<3. II: a>-2. Which conditions determine the sign of a²+a-12?
problems.idea: Factor the expression and test each condition separately.
steps: Under I alone, a=0 gives a negative value while a=-5 gives a positive one. Thus I is insufficient.
Under II alone, a=0 gives a negative value while a=4 gives a positive one. Thus II is insufficient.
Together, -2<a<3, so a+4>0 and a-3<0. The product is definitely negative.
problems.answer: Both conditions together, neither alone (option გ).

problems.title: Opposite signs rule out a radical equation
problems.question: Solve √x=-1/x.
problems.idea: Check the common domain and compare signs.
formulas: The square root needs x≥0; the reciprocal needs x≠0.
steps: Together the domain is x>0.
On this domain √x is positive and -1/x is negative.
They cannot be equal, so there are no solutions.

problems.title: Collinearity with the origin
problems.question: Points (m²,-1),(-27,m) lie on one line through the origin. Find m.
problems.idea: Their coordinate vectors must have zero determinant.
steps: The determinant is m²·m-(-1)(-27)=m³-27.
Set it to zero: m³=27.
The real solution is m=3. The two vectors are then (9,-1) and -3(9,-1).

problems.title: Area inside a midpoint square
problems.question: A square of side 2 has side midpoints E,F,G,H in order. K is the midpoint of EF. Find area KGH.
problems.idea: The midpoint figure EFGH is a square, and K lies on the side parallel to GH.
formulas: Joining side midpoints of a square forms a square with half the original area.
A triangle’s area is half base times height.
steps: The original square has area 4, so square EFGH has area 2.
EF is parallel to GH. Since K is on EF, its perpendicular distance to GH equals the height of this inner square.
Triangle KGH therefore has half the inner square area, namely 1 cm².

problems.title: A sign condition forces a positive discriminant
problems.question: If c(a+b+c)<0, compare b² and 4ac.
problems.idea: Rewrite the discriminant as a square minus the given negative quantity.
steps: The square (b+2c)² is nonnegative.
The assumption makes -4c(a+b+c) strictly positive.
Their sum is therefore strictly positive: b²-4ac>0.

problems.title: Count natural parameters for an absolute-value equation
problems.question: How many natural values of a allow |8-x|=8-a to have a solution?
problems.idea: An absolute value can equal any nonnegative real number, but never a negative one.
steps: Require 8-a≥0, hence a≤8.
Using positive natural numbers, the admissible values are 1,2,...,8.
Each works: choose x=a, for example, to make |8-a|=8-a.

problems.title: Scale the input of a quadratic
problems.question: ax²+bx+c=0 has roots -3,4. Find the larger root of (a/9)x²+(b/3)x+c=0.
problems.idea: The new polynomial is the old polynomial evaluated at x/3.
formulas: Let P(t)=at²+bt+c. Then the new equation is P(x/3)=0.
steps: We need x/3 to equal one of the original roots.
Thus x/3=-3 or x/3=4, giving x=-9 or x=12.
The larger root is 12.

problems.title: What no real roots tells us about a constant term
problems.question: ax²+bx+c=0 is quadratic and has no real roots. Also 4a+2b+c>0. What can be concluded about c from the listed choices?
problems.idea: A continuous quadratic with no zeros keeps one sign everywhere.
formulas: If a real continuous function never vanishes, it cannot change sign.
steps: The value at x=2 is positive. Since the quadratic has no real zeros, all its values are positive, including c=P(0).
However c can be less than one: P(x)=x²+1/2 meets every assumption.
It need not always be less than one, as P(x)=x²+2 also meets them.
problems.answer: c can be less than 1 (option გ); in every case c>0.

problems.title: Length of a sixty-degree angle bisector
problems.question: In a right triangle, the bisector of the 60° angle is 1 cm shorter than the longer leg. Find its length.
problems.idea: Use the 30–60–90 side ratio and the internal-bisector formula.
formulas: Bisector from angle A between sides b,c has length 2bc cos(A/2)/(b+c).
steps: The sides adjacent to 60° are t and 2t.
The bisector length is 2·t·2t·cos30°/(3t)=2√3t/3, which is two-thirds of the longer leg √3t.
The remaining one-third of the longer leg is 1 cm. Thus the longer leg is 3 cm and the bisector is 2 cm.

problems.title: Parallelogram area from adjacent angle bisectors
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, the B and C bisectors meet at M on AD. BM=10, CM=12. Find the parallelogram area.
problems.idea: Adjacent angles are supplementary, so their internal bisectors are perpendicular.
formulas: Triangle area=leg product/2 for a right triangle.
steps: In triangle BMC, the angles at B,C sum to 90°, so ∠BMC=90°.
Its area is 10·12/2=60.
Because M lies on AD∥BC, triangle BMC has the same base BC and height as the parallelogram, but half its area.
The parallelogram area is 2·60=120.

problems.title: A rectangle with trigonometric sides
problems.question: A rectangle has sides 2sinα,2cosα and area 1. Which listed angle can α equal?
problems.idea: Multiply the sides and apply the sine double-angle identity.
steps: The area condition gives sin2α=1/2.
For listed acute choices 15°,30°,45°,60°, only α=15° gives 2α=30° and sine 1/2.
Both side lengths are positive at this angle.

problems.title: Compare rectangle sides using a perimeter percentage
problems.question: A rectangle’s smaller side is 10% of its perimeter. By what percentage does the larger side exceed the smaller?
problems.idea: Convert the percentage relation into a side ratio.
steps: Multiply by 5 to get 5a=a+b, hence b=4a.
The excess is b-a=3a, or 300% of the smaller side.

problems.title: Range of a negative square root of a quadratic
problems.question: Find the range of y=-√(3x²+4x+3).
problems.idea: Complete the square to locate the smallest radicand.
steps: The radicand is at least 5/3 and can grow without bound.
Its square root ranges from √(5/3) upward.
Negating gives all values no greater than -√(5/3), including that endpoint at x=-2/3.

problems.title: A line’s angle with the vertical axis
problems.question: Line y=kx has positive k and makes an angle with the y-axis whose sine is 1/3. Find k.
problems.idea: The angle with the y-axis is complementary to the line’s acute angle with positive x.
formulas: If the vertical angle is β, slope k=cotβ=cosβ/sinβ.
steps: The angle is acute, so cosβ=√(1-1/9)=2√2/3.
Divide by sinβ=1/3.
The slope is k=2√2.

problems.title: A sum of nonnegative quantities is zero
problems.question: Find all pairs satisfying (x-2y)²+|x²-1|=0.
problems.idea: Each nonnegative summand must separately be zero.
formulas: A square and an absolute value are nonnegative.
steps: We need x-2y=0 and x²-1=0.
The second condition gives x=1 or x=-1.
From y=x/2, the pairs are (1,1/2) and (-1,-1/2).

problems.title: Two buses cover different fractions in the same time
problems.question: Two buses leave A for B together. When the first arrives, the second still has one-fifth of the route left. The first travels 20 km/h faster. Find its speed.
problems.idea: Equal travel time makes the speed ratio equal the distance ratio.
steps: The second covers four-fifths of the whole route while the first covers the whole route.
If the first speed is v, the second speed is 4v/5.
The difference v-4v/5=v/5 equals 20.
Hence v=100 km/h.

problems.title: Recover a line and a parabola from intersections
problems.question: y=kx and y=-x²+bx+c intersect at (0,0),(-4,-12). Find k,b,c.
problems.idea: Use each given point in both equations.
formulas: A point on a graph satisfies its defining equation.
steps: For the line, -12=-4k gives k=3.
The parabola passes through the origin, so c=0.

problems.title: Exactly three distinct polynomial roots
problems.question: Find all a for which (x²-5x+6)(x²-a)=0 has exactly three distinct real solutions.
problems.idea: The first factor always contributes 2,3. Count which new roots the second factor adds.
formulas: x²=a has no real roots for a<0, one for a=0, and two for a>0.
steps: For a<0 only 2,3 occur, so this case fails.
For a=0 the extra root 0 gives exactly three.
For a>0 the roots ±√a normally add two new values, giving four. Exactly one is already 2 or 3 only when √a=2 or 3.
Thus a=4 or 9 works; their negative roots add the third distinct value.

problems.title: A perpendicular segment inside a square
problems.question: ABCD is a square of side 4 cm. E∈AB, F∈BC, ∠EFD=90° and FD=5 cm. Find EF.
problems.idea: Use coordinates and enforce the right angle with a dot product.
formulas: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.
steps: FD²=16+(t-4)²=25 gives t=1; the other value 7 is outside the side.
Write E=(u,0). Then FE=(u-4,-1), FD=(-4,3). Their dot product is -4(u-4)-3=0, so u=13/4.

problems.title: Trapezoid area from two diagonal triangles
problems.question: The diagonals of trapezoid ABCD meet at O. Areas AOD and BOC are 36 and 16. Find the trapezoid area.
problems.idea: The two mixed triangles each have area equal to the geometric mean of the two base triangles.
formulas: For trapezoid bases a,b, the diagonal-intersection ratios are a:b.
steps: Triangles AOD,BOC are similar, so their corresponding length ratio is √(36/16)=3/2.
Each mixed triangle AOB,COD shares the diagonal intersection angle and has one length from each scale. Its area is √(36·16)=24.
Add all four triangles: 36+16+24+24=100.

problems.title: Two tangent semicircles along a right-triangle hypotenuse
problems.question: Two semicircles inside an isosceles right triangle have centres on its hypotenuse. They touch each other and the respective legs of length a. Find the sum of their diameters.
problems.idea: Represent both centres using their distances to the corresponding legs.
formulas: For equal legs on coordinate axes, the hypotenuse is x+y=a.
Externally tangent circles have centre distance r1+r2.
steps: Place the right vertex at (0,0). The centre near (a,0), tangent to y=0, is P=(a-r1,r1). The other centre, tangent to x=0, is Q=(r2,a-r2).
Let s=r1+r2. Because the centres are ordered along the hypotenuse, their distance is √2(a-s).
Tangency gives √2(a-s)=s. Solve s=a√2/(1+√2)=a(2-√2).
The sum of diameters is 2s=2a(2-√2), independent of how the total radius is divided between the semicircles.

problems.title: Perimeter of a trapezoid from two angles
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has bases BC,AD, ∠BCD=150°, ∠ABD=90°, BC=2 and CD=2√3. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the 30° inclination of CD to obtain the height and horizontal offset, then use the right angle at B.
formulas: Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.
steps: The trapezoid height is 2√3sin30°=√3, and CD’s horizontal projection toward D is 2√3cos30°=3.
At B, BA=(-u,-√3) and BD=(5,-√3). Their dot product is -5u+3=0, so u=3/5.
Add all four sides: P=28/5+2+2√3+2√21/5.

problems.title: Evaluate a root expression without solving for the roots
problems.question: x1,x2 are the roots of x²-5x-57=0. Evaluate 4x1²+x2²+3x1x2-15x1 without a radical answer.
problems.idea: Replace each root square using its defining quadratic.
steps: Replace the squares: 4x1²+x2²=20x1+5x2+285.
Add 3x1x2=-171 and subtract 15x1.
The result simplifies to 5x1+5x2+114.
Use the root sum: 5·5+114=139.
